assertions.description: Safe Browsing verdicts are not web-exposed: no safeBrowsing namespace exists on navigator, window, or a page-visible chrome object. This is a real privacy contract — if Chrome ever exposed a verdict surface under these names, this check would fail.
assertions.test: (() => typeof navigator.safeBrowsing === 'undefined' && !('safeBrowsing' in window) && !(typeof window.chrome === 'object' && window.chrome !== null && 'safeBrowsing' in window.chrome))()

assertions.description: No DOM event handler slot notifies a page that a suspicious site warning was shown, heeded, or bypassed: neither onsafebrowsingwarning nor onsuspicioussitewarning exists on Document.

For a user enrolled in Safe Browsing Enhanced protection, a real-time lookup verdict of SOCIAL_ENGINEERING with verdict type WARN surfaces a bypassable pop-up that must be acknowledged before continuing.
assertions.test: Not run automatically: requires enrollment in Enhanced protection, the SuspiciousSiteWarnings base::Feature enabled, and Google's server-side real-time lookup returning a WARN verdict for a visited URL — none of which a showcase page can produce or observe. Verify per the Field Verification Lab via chrome://safe-browsing.

assertions.description: The suspicious site warning is nonblocking: SB_THREAT_TYPE_WARNABLE_SUSPICIOUS_SITE (29) is documented as 'a nonblocking warning' and is not associated with an interstitial — the navigation is not replaced and the page continues to load behind the pop-up.
assertions.test: Not run automatically: observing the loaded-page-behind-popup state requires a real WARN verdict in a real Chrome session. Contract pinned by the SBThreatType comment in sb_protocol_manager_util.h and the interstitial-exclusion lists in security_state utils.

assertions.description: The warning is additive: confirmed malicious sites (DANGEROUS verdicts / blocklist hits) continue to show the blocking red interstitial at Standard and Enhanced protection levels.
assertions.test: Not run automatically: triggering a real interstitial requires visiting a flagged site (e.g. the pages linked from testsafebrowsing.appspot.com) in a Safe Browsing-enabled Chrome; a showcase page cannot host confirmed-threat content.

assertions.description: The behavior is gated on the SuspiciousSiteWarnings base::Feature: with it disabled, the identical SOCIAL_ENGINEERING + WARN verdict maps to SB_THREAT_TYPE_SAFE and the user sees nothing.
assertions.test: Not run automatically: base::Feature state is browser-process-only and unobservable from a page. Contract pinned by url_lookup_service_unittest.cc (GetSBThreatTypeForRTThreatType expectations with the feature enabled vs disabled); verify manually by comparing runs with and without --enable-features=SuspiciousSiteWarnings.

assertions.description: Admins control the warning with SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel (only level 2, EnhancedProtection, can produce it; levels 0-1 cannot) and suppress it per-domain with SafeBrowsingAllowlistDomains, whose domain-suffix entries exempt matching hosts from Safe Browsing checks entirely.
assertions.test: Not run automatically: policy values are not readable from page JavaScript. Verify on a managed machine at chrome://policy, per the Enterprise Policy Lab and the chromeenterprise.google policy documentation for SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel and SafeBrowsingAllowlistDomains.
